# Curriculum

One folder per module: `mNN-slug/` holds the module guide (`README.md`) and its labs
(`lab_NNx_topic.py`). The structure, weeks and lab status come from
[`course/course.yaml`](../course/course.yaml); the tables here are generated.

\*On a typical laptop, one process. Planned labs have a written specification in their module
guide and are replaced by an exercise pack until they ship.

## Every module guide has the same sections

| Section | What it contains |
|---|---|
| Header (generated) | Term, weeks, hours, labs, library modules, prerequisites, committed topics, status |
| Why this module | The problem it solves and how later modules depend on it |
| Learning outcomes | Measurable outcomes |
| Before you start | Prerequisites, readings and setup |
| Weekly plan | One table per week: every session (L1, L2, C1, OH, C2, QP, self-study) with minute-by-minute time boxes |
| Labs | Sections, what learners do, and what good results look like; specifications for planned labs |
| Assessment | Quizzes, lab, assignment with rubric and due date |
| Common mistakes | Typical errors and how the module catches them |
| Readings | Books and papers |
| Instructor notes | Owner, refresh duties, pitfalls |

The route manager checks that every guide has these sections and a plan for each of its weeks.

## Running labs

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,boost]"                            # or: pip install -r requirements.txt
python curriculum/m10-trading-strategies/lab_10a_trading_strategies.py
make labs                                                # every ready lab as a smoke test
```

Labs are Jupytext "percent" scripts: run them as scripts or open them as notebooks
(`pip install jupytext`, then *Open With → Notebook*). Charts go to `build/lab-output/`
(`CFMAT_OUTPUT_DIR` overrides it).

Every lab runs offline on synthetic or fictional data. Several data generators plant a known effect
so a method can be seen working when the effect exists — say so when you teach them, and repeat the
exercise on real data. Optional extras: `xgboost`, `lightgbm` and `optuna` for M23 (sections are
skipped if absent); `yfinance` for real prices; `anthropic` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the LLM step
in M22 (`claude-opus-5` unless `CFMAT_CLAUDE_MODEL` names another model); `torch` for the M20 LSTM
exercise.
